paragraphs: An outbreak of E. coli and Salmonella linked to alfalfa sprouts remains ongoing, with 76 cases and 6 hospitalizations reported across 16 states [1]. Two other outbreaks have ended: a Salmonella outbreak tied to jalapeños affected 488 people across 34 states [2], and an E. coli O145 outbreak from frozen blueberries sickened 17 people in 2 states [3].

A Class I recall for ineligible pork cracklings has been issued for 60-gram foil bags of "YUPI GOLPE CON TODO SABOR BBQ" mixed chips sold in Arizona, California, Colorado, Florida, Illinois, Kentucky, Minnesota, and Texas [4]. The USDA also issued a public health alert for 140-gram cans of "GRACE READY TO EAT CHICKEN VIENNA SAUSAGES" imported illegally from Jamaica and found in Alabama, Florida, Georgia, Maryland, and Texas [5].

Eden Brothers is recalling Calabrese Broccoli Seeds in 1-ounce and 1-pound packet sizes due to possible Salmonella contamination [6]. EAK Distribution recalled HOME GROWN Green Sprouting Calabrese Broccoli Seeds, 8 ounces, for the same reason [10]. Additional lots of frozen berry products have been recalled for potential E. coli O145 contamination, including Great Value Frozen Organic Triple Berry Blend and Blueberries, and Trader Joe's Frozen Organic Mixed Berry Blend [11]. Nature's Own Hawaiian Bread in 20 and 40 ounce bags has been recalled for undeclared milk [12], Saint Francis Apizza frozen pizzas for undeclared soy allergen [15], and Stewart's Shops ice cream in Heavenly Medley and Vanilla-Chocolate-Strawberry flavors (half-gallon size) for potential metal contamination [9].
